subject: slow warmup with NUTS II; step size vs. mass matrix

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: slow warmup with NUTS II; step size vs. mass matrix
parts:
Why is NUTS II set up to adapt both step size
and a diagonal mass matrix? With a diagonal mass
matrix, adapting the step size seems redundant
(in a redundant parameterization kind of way).
I'm wondering if it's causing the practical problem
we're having (see example below).

Should I instead have the options instead be:

1. fixed epsilon
2. optimize epsilon as in NUTS I
3. estimate diagonal mass matrix as in NUTS II

Or at least issue a warning about turning on both
epsilon optimization and mass matrix estimation?

The practical problem arises with the very simple normal
sampling model with NUTS II:

parameters {
real y;
}
model {
y ~ normal(0,1);
}

With 1000 warmup iterations and 1000 samples, what
often happens is that the chain moves slowly around the
mode (here the origin) and then gets stuck when it
gets 2 standard deviations away from the mode with an
effectively 100% rejection rate.

With 5000 warmup iterations and 5000 samples, the
problem seems to go away for some reason.

Also, if I set epsilon to a fixed value, I don't
run into the problem.

- Bob

messages.author: 1004dd6f66bb10c3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] slow warmup with NUTS II; step size vs. mass matrix
parts:
Right the first time, it's adapting step size and the diagonal mass
matrix. The mass vector is constrained to have unit norm, so as to
roughly orthogonalize the issues of preconditioning and step size
adaptation. Step size adaptation happens every iteration of warmup,
whereas the mass matrix gets updated only after the 10th, 20th, 40th,
80th, etc. steps.

That the normal(0, 1) case doesn't work is troubling. I'll look into it.

Matt
